reason: I want to bring the first specimen home, and placing it in the flight locker seems like a useful first step.
expectation: I expect the membrane to be placed in the locker, though it may need another action to secure it.

alternatives.reason: Harvesting lettuce seems relevant to taking some of the garden along, but I want to attend to the specimen first.

effect: Placing the membrane in the flight locker completed the specimen goal, so I can turn to the garden.
reaction: It was reassuring that the specimen was ready to travel without another step.
reason: Cutting lettuce is the only available combination and seems like a way to take some of the garden along.
expectation: I expect to harvest the new leaves, perhaps for packing at the flight galley.

effect: The leaves are harvested and ready to take to the lander’s galley.
reaction: The familiar scissors and bare calendar mark the departure poignantly.
reason: The galley is the only available combination and should fulfill the goal of taking garden produce along.
expectation: I expect the lettuce to be placed or prepared in the flight galley, completing the garden goal.

effect: Packing the lettuce into a flight meal completed the garden goal and the chapter.
reaction: The handful of green is a satisfying reminder of the garden that survived the storm.

mostWorthwhile.text: Packing the lettuce for the flight was most worthwhile: it gave the departure a tangible connection to the garden.

leastWorthwhile.text: Placing the membrane in the locker felt brief and mechanical, although its purpose was clear.

surprise.text: I expected the membrane might need another securing step, but placing it at the locker completed its goal.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though harvesting and packing the lettuce were the only available combinations at their respective steps.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see what the receiving lab learns from the specimens, and the departure makes me interested in what comes next.
